page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this configuration, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a capable compute profile with some single-core limitations. The stress-ng single-core CPU test ranks in the top 25% with a score of 2680.97, while multi-core performance falls in the middle 50% at 21496.93. Geekbench scores show average multi-core capabilities of 5488.0 but poor single-core performance of 858.0, a trend mirrored by poor single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 71.67 GB/sec for large block uncached reads and 35.27 GB/sec for writes.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is designed for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It achieves average performance in database operations with a Passmark score of 4820.33, static web serving at 12.91 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations at 15.91 million operations per second. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads like software compilation, basic web serving, and lightweight LLM inference where CPU core density is prioritized over memory capacity.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 compute-focused instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. Lacking bundled local storage or GPUs, this server is tailored for workloads requiring higher CPU density relative to memory. Benchmark results show strong single-core stress-ng performance, though overall single-threaded execution in compression tasks is weak. Multi-core benchmarks, including Geekbench and Passmark CPU tests, consistently rank in the average tier. With a 1:1 GB-to-vCPU ratio, this instance offers a cost-effective profile for parallelizable, compute-bound tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, and Redis operations, where massive memory allocations are unnecessary.
